description: The SpecterOps BloodHound GitHub saved-query corpus, translated to Gryphon for the TAP grid. One record per BloodHound query id; `sources` carries every upstream variant verbatim with its pinned commit. `status`/`stage` say whether and when the translation runs on a grid collected by github_core. Content, not fixture data: no nodes, no expected rows.
license: Apache-2.0 — SpecterOps; names, descriptions and Cypher reproduced with attribution

stages.today: runs on a grid github_core has collected
stages.A: after github-core#110 — organization, repository and environment settings in configuration
stages.A2: after github-core#114 — ruleset rules flattened to configuration.rule_types
stages.B: after github-core#111 — members, teams, membership and repository grants
stages.C: after github-core#112 — custom organization roles and fine-grained PAT grants
stages.na: not observable for a Team-plan organization (Enterprise, SAML/SCIM, another cloud's identity graph)

queries.name: Actions SHA Pinning Not Required
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds organizations that do not require SHA pinning for GitHub Actions. Without pinning, actions referenced by tag can be silently replaced with malicious versions.
queries.about: Whether the organization forces every `uses:` to a full commit SHA. Without it a tag can be moved under a workflow — the tj-actions/changed-files shape.
gryphon: RETURN a.data.login AS organization, a.data.configuration.settings_observability AS settings_observed, a.data.configuration.actions_policy.sha_pinning_required AS sha_pinning_required
queries.caveat: An organization whose policy block the credential could not read carries no such key and does not match — its `settings_observed` reads `public_only` or `unobservable` on the organization's own page. Absence of a row is not a clean bill.

queries.name: Active Leaked Secrets
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds secret scanning alerts that are both unresolved and confirmed active. These are valid, usable credentials committed to source code and represent an immediate compromise risk.
queries.about: Open alerts GitHub has confirmed as live credentials. BloodHound's collector proves liveness by *using* the leaked token; TAP will read GitHub's `validity` field and never touch the credential.
queries.hatch: none — same collector build as secret-scanning-alerts; `validity` is a field on the alert GitHub returns

queries.name: Advanced Security Disabled for New Repositories
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds organizations where GitHub Advanced Security is not automatically enabled for new repositories. New repositories will lack code scanning, secret scanning, and other GHAS features.
queries.about: Whether new repositories inherit GitHub Advanced Security. Off means each new repository starts without code scanning.
gryphon: RETURN a.data.login AS organization, a.data.configuration.settings_observability AS settings_observed, a.data.configuration.advanced_security_enabled_for_new_repositories AS advanced_security_enabled_for_new_repositories
queries.caveat: An organization whose policy block the credential could not read carries no such key and does not match — its `settings_observed` reads `public_only` or `unobservable` on the organization's own page. Absence of a row is not a clean bill.

queries.name: All GitHub Actions Allowed
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds organizations that allow all GitHub Actions to run, including third-party actions from the marketplace. This creates supply chain risk if a malicious or compromised action is used.
queries.about: Whether any marketplace action may run. `all` is the default and the widest supply-chain surface; `selected` names an allow-list.
gryphon: RETURN a.data.login AS organization, a.data.configuration.settings_observability AS settings_observed, a.data.configuration.actions_policy.allowed_actions AS allowed_actions
queries.caveat: An organization whose policy block the credential could not read carries no such key and does not match — its `settings_observed` reads `public_only` or `unobservable` on the organization's own page. Absence of a row is not a clean bill.

queries.name: App Installations with Access to All Repositories
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds GitHub App installations that have access to every repository in the organization. A compromised app credential would affect all repositories.
queries.about: App installations that follow the organization into every repository, present and future.
gryphon: RETURN i.data.app_slug AS app, i.data.account_login AS account, i.data.permissions AS permissions, i.data.suspended AS suspended

queries.name: Branch Protection Rules - Admins Not Enforced
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds branch protection rules where administrators can bypass all protections. Admins can push directly, skip reviews, and override status checks on these branches.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(:GH_BranchProtectionRule {enforce_admins: false})-[:GH_ProtectedBy]->(:GH_Branch)
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Rulesets an organization administrator may bypass outright.
gryphon: RETURN rs.data.owner_login AS owner, rs.data.name AS ruleset, rs.data.enforcement AS enforcement, b.data.name AS branch, b.data.is_default AS is_default
queries.caveat: GitHub rulesets replaced classic branch protection; the rule set is a LIST on the ruleset node, and Gryphon has no array-membership predicate, so github-core#114 flattens it into `configuration.rule_types` first. A branch under no ruleset at all is a different query (unprotected-branches).

queries.name: Users Who Can Bypass Pull Request Requirements
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds users and teams that can bypass pull request review requirements on protected branches. These actors can merge code without any reviews.
queries.about: Who may bypass a ruleset. GitHub discloses bypass actors only to a writer of the ruleset; the grid draws an edge for each App it could name, counts the rest on the ruleset (`bypass_actor_count`), and keeps teams and roles in `bypass_actors_unmodelled` until the people graph gives them nodes.
gryphon: RETURN rs.data.owner_login AS owner, rs.data.name AS ruleset, actor.name AS actor, e.data.properties.actor_type AS actor_type, e.data.properties.bypass_mode AS bypass_mode, rs.data.bypass_observability AS bypass_observed, rs.data.bypass_actor_count AS bypass_actors
queries.caveat: Zero rows with a non-zero `bypass_actors` means the actors exist and were not nameable, not that nobody may bypass.

queries.name: Dangerous Branch Permissions

gryphon: RETURN u.data.login AS user, r.data.full_name AS repository, p.data.properties.permission AS permission
queries.hatch: module runner: WITH RECURSIVE over MEMBER_OF_TEAM / NESTED_IN_TEAM / HAS_REPO_PERMISSION on the read-only alias, depth cap, cycle guard; direct HAS_REPO_PERMISSION rows unioned in

queries.name: Organizations with default repository permission
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns organizations that have a default repository permission other than 'none'.

sources.cypher:
MATCH (o:GH_Organization)
WHERE o.default_repository_permission <> 'none'
RETURN o
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: The permission every member holds on every repository by default. Anything but `none` is a grant nobody wrote down per repository.
gryphon: RETURN a.data.login AS organization, a.data.configuration.settings_observability AS settings_observed, a.data.configuration.default_repository_permission AS default_repository_permission
queries.caveat: An organization whose policy block the credential could not read carries no such key and does not match — its `settings_observed` reads `public_only` or `unobservable` on the organization's own page. Absence of a row is not a clean bill.

queries.name: [Demo] SSO Round-Trip: Azure/Okta → GitHub → Cloud Identity
queries.bloodhound_description: The cloud-to-cloud pivot through GitHub: a compromised Azure or Okta identity syncs to a GitHub user via SSO. That GitHub user has write access to repositories configured with OIDC federation to Azure workload identities. The attacker pivots from one cloud identity through GitHub into a completely different Azure identity — crossing cloud boundaries twice in a single attack chain.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p1=(extUser)-[:SyncedToGHUser]->(ghUser:GH_User)
MATCH p2=(ghUser)-[:GH_HasRole|GH_HasBaseRole|GH_MemberOf*1..]->(:GH_RepoRole)-[:GH_WriteRepoContents]->(:GH_Repository)-[:GH_CanAssumeIdentity]->(cred:AZFederatedIdentityCredential)
RETURN p1, p2
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: The cloud-to-cloud pivot through GitHub. Its GitHub half (write access → OIDC federation) is `secrets-reachable-by-user` plus `github-to-azure-identity`; the identity-provider half needs SSO.

queries.name: GitHub-to-Azure Identity Assumptions

queries.about: Repositories whose OIDC subject a cloud trusts. The grid keeps the evidence chain (repository → identity provider → issuer) where BloodHound draws one computed `CanAssumeIdentity` edge; the conclusion is a query over the chain.
gryphon: RETURN r.data.full_name AS repository, p.name AS provider, p.entity_type AS provider_type
queries.caveat: AWS only today (aws_core's IAM OIDC providers); Azure federated credentials have no plugin. Zero rows on a grid without aws_core is `not observable`, not `no federation`.

queries.name: Global Repo Permissions
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all users who hold a global repository permission role (i.e., roles that are not default).

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(:GH_User)-[:GH_HasBaseRole|GH_HasRole|GH_MemberOf*1..3]->(role:GH_OrgRole)
WHERE role.short_name CONTAINS 'all_repo_'
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Users holding an all-repository role (`all_repo_admin`, `all_repo_write`, …) — GitHub's synthetic roles behind custom organization roles.
queries.hatch: once roles land: a one-hop filter on HOLDS_ORG_ROLE suffices for direct holders; the `*1..3` in the corpus covers base-role inheritance, which a module runner walks

queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all custom organization roles that are privileged (i.e., have permissions that are not default)

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(role:GH_OrgRole {type:'custom'})-[r]->(dest)
WHERE dest:GH_Organization
OR dest:GH_OrgRole
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Custom organization roles and the permissions they grant. Our org has none; the App already holds the permission to list them.
gryphon: RETURN role.data.name AS role, role.data.base_role AS base_role, role.data.permissions AS permissions

queries.name: Privileged Hybrid Identities
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all hybrid identities (e.g., Azure or Okta users) that are associated with GitHub users who hold the organization owners role.
queries.about: Identity-provider identities mapped to owners. Needs SAML SSO, which a Team-plan organization does not have.
needs: SAML / SCIM external identities — Enterprise or SSO-enabled organizations only

queries.name: Public Repositories
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all public repositories.
queries.about: Every public repository. Not a finding on its own; the set everything public-facing is measured against.
gryphon: RETURN r.data.full_name AS repository, r.data.default_branch AS default_branch, r.data.configuration.archived AS archived

queries.name: Secret Scanning Push Protection Disabled for New Repositories
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds organizations where push protection is not enabled for new repositories. Without push protection, secrets can be committed without being blocked before they reach the repository.
queries.about: Whether pushes containing a detected secret are blocked in new repositories.
gryphon: RETURN a.data.login AS organization, a.data.configuration.settings_observability AS settings_observed, a.data.configuration.secret_scanning_push_protection_enabled_for_new_repositories AS secret_scanning_push_protection_enabled_for_new_repositories
queries.caveat: An organization whose policy block the credential could not read carries no such key and does not match — its `settings_observed` reads `public_only` or `unobservable` on the organization's own page. Absence of a row is not a clean bill.

queries.name: Users Who Can Push to Protected Branches
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds users and teams that are allowed to push directly to protected branches when push restrictions are enabled. These actors bypass the normal pull request workflow.
queries.about: Actors who may push past a ruleset unconditionally (`bypass_mode: always`), as opposed to only through a pull request.
gryphon: RETURN rs.data.owner_login AS owner, rs.data.name AS ruleset, actor.name AS actor, e.data.properties.actor_type AS actor_type
queries.caveat: Same disclosure ceiling as bypass-pr-requirements.

queries.name: Repositories with Secret Scanning Disabled
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds repositories where secret scanning is disabled. Committed credentials in these repositories will not be detected by GitHub.
queries.about: Repositories where secret scanning is off. GitHub omits the whole security block for a non-admin caller, so a repository whose `security_settings_observability` is `unobservable` is missing from this list without being clean.
gryphon: RETURN r.data.full_name AS repository, r.data.visibility AS visibility, r.data.configuration.archived AS archived

queries.name: Repos Vulnerable to Workflow Secret Exfiltration
queries.bloodhound_description: Secrets reachable by users who can create new branches (computed by Compute-GitHoundBranchAccess). The GH_CanCreateBranch edge accounts for branch protection rules, push restrictions, blocks_creations settings, and all bypass mechanisms (admin, push_protected_branch, pushAllowances). Edges emit from RepoRole in the common case; per-actor edges from User/Team are only present when per-rule allowances grant additional access beyond the role.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p1=(:GH_User)-[:GH_HasRole|GH_HasBaseRole|GH_MemberOf*1..]->(:GH_RepoRole)-[:GH_CanCreateBranch]->(repo:GH_Repository)-[:GH_HasSecret]->(s)
WHERE (s:GH_RepoSecret
OR s:GH_OrgSecret)
OPTIONAL MATCH p2=(repo)<-[:GH_CanCreateBranch]-(:GH_User)
OPTIONAL MATCH p3=(repo)<-[:GH_CanCreateBranch]-(:GH_Team)<-[:GH_HasRole|GH_MemberOf|GH_AddMember*1..]-(:GH_User)
RETURN p1, p2, p3
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Secrets reachable by anyone who can create a branch and push a workflow to it. BloodHound pre-computes `CanCreateBranch` from rulesets, push restrictions and bypasses; that derivation is the work.
blocked_on: a derived branch-creation edge (rulesets + bypass) that nothing computes yet
queries.hatch: the reachability runner plus a Python judgement over ruleset `creation` rules and bypass actors — a conclusion edge, which the vocabulary says to derive, not collect

queries.name: Repository Workflows
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all repository workflows
queries.about: Every workflow file, by repository. The inventory the Actions half of the corpus is measured against.
gryphon: RETURN r.data.full_name AS repository, w.data.path AS workflow, w.data.state AS state, w.data.workflow_id AS workflow_id

queries.name: SAML Configuration Mapping
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds SAML Identity Providers, their external identities, and mapped users.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(OIP:GH_SamlIdentityProvider)-[:GH_HasExternalIdentity]->(EI:GH_ExternalIdentity)
MATCH p1=(OIP)<-[:GH_HasSamlIdentityProvider]-(:GH_Organization)
MATCH p2=(EI)-[:GH_MapsToUser]->()
RETURN p,p1,p2
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: SAML identity providers, their external identities and mapped users.

queries.name: Secret Scanning Alerts
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all repositories that have secret scanning alerts.
queries.about: Repositories with open secret-scanning alerts — committed credentials GitHub found.
needs: secret_scanning_alert detail node behind compliance_core__compliance_finding — the code-scanning pattern; App permission secret_scanning_alerts not granted
queries.hatch: none that is honest — the alert listing must be collected first (github_core, `/repos/{r}/secret-scanning/alerts`, App permission secret_scanning_alerts); a module cannot conjure data the grid does not hold

queries.name: Secret Scanning Disabled for New Repositories
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds organizations where secret scanning is not automatically enabled for new repositories. New repositories will not detect committed credentials until manually enabled.
queries.about: Whether secret scanning is on for new repositories.
gryphon: RETURN a.data.login AS organization, a.data.configuration.settings_observability AS settings_observed, a.data.configuration.secret_scanning_enabled_for_new_repositories AS secret_scanning_enabled_for_new_repositories
queries.caveat: An organization whose policy block the credential could not read carries no such key and does not match — its `settings_observed` reads `public_only` or `unobservable` on the organization's own page. Absence of a row is not a clean bill.

queries.name: Secrets Reachable by User
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all repo and org secrets reachable by users through write access. Users with write access can create GitHub Actions workflows to access secrets.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(:GH_User)-[:GH_HasRole|GH_HasBaseRole|GH_MemberOf*1..]->(:GH_RepoRole)-[:GH_WriteRepoContents]->(:GH_Repository)-[:GH_HasSecret]->(s)
WHERE s:GH_RepoSecret
OR s:GH_OrgSecret
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Which secrets a user could read by writing a workflow. Write access to a repository is read access to every secret its workflows can name — the finding the secrets page hints at, asked from the person's side.
gryphon: RETURN u.data.login AS user, r.data.full_name AS repository, s.data.name AS secret
queries.hatch: the reachability runner, extended one hop to DEFINES_SECRET; organization secrets join through their `visibility` (all / private / selected)

queries.name: Self-Hosted Runners Can Intercept Broad-Token Jobs
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns self-hosted runners that can intercept workflow jobs whose effective GITHUB_TOKEN has high-impact write permissions. These jobs can materially increase the blast radius of runner compromise.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(runner:GH_Runner)-[:GH_CanInterceptJob]->(job:GH_WorkflowJob)
WHERE 'contents:write' IN job.effective_github_token_permissions
OR 'actions:write' IN job.effective_github_token_permissions
OR 'pull-requests:write' IN job.effective_github_token_permissions
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: The subset of interceptable jobs whose token has write on contents, Actions or pull requests.
queries.hatch: same runner as workflow-jobs-interceptable-by-self-hosted-runners, filtered on declared write permissions

queries.name: Shared Self-Hosted Runners Can Intercept Secret-Bearing Jobs
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns organization- and enterprise-scoped self-hosted runners that can intercept workflow jobs with statically resolvable secret access. Shared runners are especially important to review because compromise can expose execution contexts across multiple repositories.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(runner:GH_Runner)-[:GH_CanInterceptJob]->(job:GH_WorkflowJob)-[:GH_CanAccessSecret]->(secret:GH_Secret)
WHERE runner:GH_OrgRunner
OR runner:GH_EnterpriseRunner
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Shared runners reaching jobs that read secrets. Runner groups are an organization/enterprise surface the collector does not read yet.
needs: organization- and enterprise-scoped runners (runner groups) — not collected; enterprise not on this plan

queries.name: Tier Zero All-Repo Admin Role
queries.bloodhound_description: The synthetic all_repo_admin role grants admin access to every repository in the organization. This role is inherited by the owners role via GH_HasBaseRole and cascades admin permissions including branch protection editing, secret access, and deploy key management to all repositories.

sources.cypher: MATCH (n:GH_OrgRole) WHERE n.name CONTAINS 'ALL_REPO_ADMIN' RETURN n

queries.about: The synthetic all-repository-admin role that the owners role inherits.
gryphon: RETURN role.data.name AS role, role.data.source AS source

queries.name: Tier Zero App Installations (All Repositories)
queries.bloodhound_description: GitHub App installations scoped to all repositories in the organization that have at least one write permission. A compromised app credential grants write access to every repository. Installations with only read permissions are excluded — they pose a data exfiltration risk but do not grant control over the organization.

sources.cypher:
MATCH (n:GH_AppInstallation {repository_selection:'all'})
WHERE n.permissions CONTAINS '"write"'
RETURN n

MATCH (n:GH_AppInstallation {repository_selection:'all'})
WHERE ANY(permission IN n.permissions WHERE permission IN ['contents:write', 'administration:write', 'workflows:write', 'actions:write'])
RETURN n

queries.about: All-repository installations holding a write permission that matters — contents, administration, workflows or Actions. A leaked installation credential is a write to every repository.
gryphon: WHERE i.data.repository_selection = "all" AND (i.data.permissions.contents = "write" OR i.data.permissions.administration = "write" OR i.data.permissions.workflows = "write" OR i.data.permissions.actions = "write")
RETURN i.data.app_slug AS app, i.data.account_login AS account, i.data.permissions AS permissions

queries.name: Tier Zero Apps (All-Repository Installations)
queries.bloodhound_description: GitHub App definitions whose installations have write access to all repositories. The app owner controls the private key that can generate tokens for any installation. Compromise of the app's private key grants write access to every repository in organizations where it is installed. Apps whose installations have only read permissions are excluded.

sources.cypher:
MATCH (n:GH_App)-[:GH_InstalledAs]->(i:GH_AppInstallation {repository_selection:'all'})
WHERE i.permissions CONTAINS '"write"'
RETURN n

MATCH (n:GH_App)-[:GH_InstalledAs]->(i:GH_AppInstallation {repository_selection:'all'})
WHERE ANY(permission IN i.permissions WHERE permission IN ['contents:write', 'administration:write', 'workflows:write', 'actions:write'])
RETURN n

queries.about: The Apps behind those installations — whoever holds the App's private key can mint a token for every installation.
gryphon: WHERE i.data.repository_selection = "all" AND (i.data.permissions.contents = "write" OR i.data.permissions.administration = "write" OR i.data.permissions.workflows = "write" OR i.data.permissions.actions = "write")
RETURN app.data.slug AS app, app.data.name AS name, i.data.account_login AS account

queries.name: Tier Zero Enterprise Owners Role
queries.bloodhound_description: The enterprise owners role grants administrative control over the GitHub Enterprise account, including enterprise organizations, members, identity provider configuration, and enterprise-wide security settings.
queries.about: The enterprise owners role.

queries.name: Tier Zero External Identities (Owner-Mapped)
queries.bloodhound_description: External identities from SAML/SCIM providers that map to GitHub users holding the owners role. Compromise of these external identities in the identity provider grants organizational owner access to GitHub via SSO.
queries.about: External identities mapped to owners.

queries.name: Tier Zero Organizations
queries.bloodhound_description: GitHub organizations are the root trust boundary for all repositories, teams, users, and settings. Compromise of the organization grants full administrative control over all contained assets.
queries.about: The organizations on the grid — BloodHound's Tier Zero root. Everything else hangs off these.
gryphon: RETURN a.data.login AS organization, a.data.configuration.plan.name AS plan, a.data.configuration.two_factor_requirement_enabled AS two_factor_required, a.data.configuration.settings_observability AS settings_observed

queries.name: Tier Zero Owner Users
queries.bloodhound_description: Users who hold the organization owners role have full administrative control over the GitHub organization. Compromise of any owner account grants control over all repositories, secrets, SSO configuration, and cloud identities.
queries.about: Tier Zero: the accounts whose compromise is the organization's compromise.
gryphon: RETURN u.data.login AS user, o.data.login AS organization

queries.name: Tier Zero Owners Role
queries.bloodhound_description: The owners organization role grants full administrative control including all repository admin, member management, SSO configuration, app management, and billing. Owners inherit all_repo_admin, cascading admin access to every repository, secret, environment, and cloud identity in the organization.
queries.about: The owners role as an object. With roles as edge properties there is no node to return; the honest equivalent is the owner count per organization.
gryphon: RETURN o.data.login AS organization, COUNT(u) AS owners

queries.name: Tier Zero PATs (All Repositories)
queries.bloodhound_description: Fine-grained personal access tokens scoped to all repositories in the organization that have at least one write permission. A single compromised token grants write access to every repository. PATs with only read permissions are excluded — they pose a data exfiltration risk but do not grant control over the organization.

sources.cypher:
MATCH (n:GH_PersonalAccessToken {repository_selection:'all'})
WHERE n.permissions CONTAINS '"write"'
RETURN n

MATCH (n:GH_PersonalAccessToken {repository_selection:'all'})
WHERE ANY(permission IN n.repository_permissions WHERE permission IN ['contents:write', 'administration:write', 'workflows:write', 'actions:write'])
RETURN n

queries.about: All-repository tokens with a write that matters — one token, every repository.
gryphon: WHERE g.data.kind = "pat" AND g.data.repository_selection = "all" AND (g.data.permissions.contents = "write" OR g.data.permissions.administration = "write" OR g.data.permissions.workflows = "write" OR g.data.permissions.actions = "write")
RETURN u.data.login AS owner, g.data.name AS token, g.data.permissions AS permissions

queries.name: Tier Zero Privilege Escalation Roles
queries.bloodhound_description: Custom organization roles with write_organization_custom_org_role permission can modify organization role definitions, including setting the base_role to inherit all_repo_admin. Since this permission only exists on custom organization roles, the holder can escalate the role they already hold — a guaranteed self-escalation path to full organizational control.
queries.about: Roles that may rewrite custom roles, including themselves.
gryphon: RETURN role.data.name AS role, role.data.source AS source
queries.caveat: Written as a text CONTAINS over the permission list; a map shape (`permissions.write_organization_custom_org_role = true`) is the better model and is one of #112's questions.

queries.name: Tier Zero Privilege Escalation Users
queries.bloodhound_description: Users who hold custom organization roles with write_organization_custom_org_role permission. These users can modify organization role definitions — including the role they hold — to set the base_role to all_repo_admin, granting themselves admin access to every repository in the organization.
queries.about: Users whose custom role may edit custom roles — a self-escalation to owner.
queries.hatch: one-hop filter for direct holders; base-role inheritance via the runner

queries.name: Tier Zero SAML Identity Providers
queries.bloodhound_description: SAML identity providers control authentication for all organization members via SSO. Compromise of the identity provider grants the ability to impersonate any user, including organization owners, by manipulating SAML assertions or resetting credentials.
queries.about: The identity providers that authenticate members.

queries.name: Team Membership Admins
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all users who hold the maintainer role over a team, this also represents team nesting.
queries.about: Team maintainers — the people who can add members, and through nesting, to the child teams too. The nested half is BloodHound's second, correlated clause (tap#433); the direct half is a filter.
gryphon: RETURN t.data.slug AS team, u.data.login AS maintainer, t.data.parent_slug AS parent_team

queries.name: Team Structure
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns the structure of teams within organizations, including team roles and their members.
queries.about: Who is on which team, with what role, and the team's parent. BloodHound walks the nesting with `*1..`; one level is a field here, deeper nesting waits on tap#259 or the reachability runner.
gryphon: RETURN t.data.slug AS team, t.data.parent_slug AS parent_team, u.data.login AS member, m.data.properties.role AS role

queries.name: Unprotected Branches
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all unprotected branches in repositories.
queries.about: Branches no ruleset protects. Feature branches are expected here; a default or release branch is not.
gryphon: RETURN g.data.full_name AS repository, b.data.name AS branch, b.data.is_default AS is_default

queries.name: Repositories with Workflows and Unprotected Default Branch
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all repositories that have GitHub Actions workflows and an unprotected default branch. This means that users with GH_WriteRepoContents to the Repository can overwrite or change the workflow.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(repo:GH_Repository)-[:GH_HasWorkflow]->(:GH_Workflow)
MATCH p1=(repo)-[:GH_HasBranch]->(branch:GH_Branch)
WHERE repo.default_branch = branch.short_name
RETURN p1
LIMIT 1000

MATCH p=(repo:GH_Repository)-[:GH_Contains]->(:GH_Workflow)
MATCH p1=(repo)-[:GH_Contains]->(branch:GH_Branch)
WHERE repo.default_branch = branch.short_name
AND branch.protected = false
RETURN p1
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Repositories that both run workflows and leave their default branch unprotected — so a write can also rewrite the automation. BloodHound writes this as two correlated clauses; one chain through the repository says the same thing.
gryphon: RETURN g.data.full_name AS repository, b.data.name AS branch, w.data.path AS workflow

queries.name: Unprotected Default Branches
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns all default branches in repositories that are not protected.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(repo:GH_Repository)-[:GH_HasBranch]-(branch:GH_Branch {protected: false})
WHERE repo.default_branch = branch.short_name
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

MATCH p=(repo:GH_Repository)-[:GH_Contains]-(branch:GH_Branch {protected: false})
WHERE repo.default_branch = branch.short_name
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Default branches with no ruleset in front of them: anyone with write can push straight to what everyone builds from. BloodHound needs a property-to-property comparison here; `git_ref.is_default` makes it a filter.
gryphon: RETURN g.data.full_name AS repository, b.data.name AS branch

queries.name: Web Commit Signoff Not Required
queries.bloodhound_description: Finds organizations that do not require sign-off for web-based commits. Without signoff, commit attribution cannot be verified.
queries.about: Whether commits made in the web editor must carry a sign-off.
gryphon: RETURN a.data.login AS organization, a.data.configuration.settings_observability AS settings_observed, a.data.configuration.web_commit_signoff_required AS web_commit_signoff_required
queries.caveat: An organization whose policy block the credential could not read carries no such key and does not match — its `settings_observed` reads `public_only` or `unobservable` on the organization's own page. Absence of a row is not a clean bill.

queries.name: Workflow Jobs Interceptable by Self-Hosted Runners
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns workflow jobs whose future execution context may be exposed to an actor controlling a collected self-hosted runner that is not explicitly marked ephemeral.
queries.about: Jobs a self-hosted runner could pick up. The grid records the observed fact (`EXECUTED_ON_RUNNER`), not the eligibility; the eligibility is a label-set comparison the module hatch can do today.
needs: a derived RUNS_ON eligibility edge (runner labels ⊇ job runs-on, non-ephemeral)
blocked_on: derived eligibility edge not built (vocabulary: runner_group / MEMBER_OF_RUNNER_GROUP are friends-tier)
queries.hatch: a module runner that intersects `github_runner.labels` with `workflow_job.runs_on` in Python and returns the pairs as edges

queries.name: Workflow Jobs with Broad GITHUB_TOKEN Write Permissions
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns workflow jobs whose calculated effective GITHUB_TOKEN permissions include write access to repository contents, Actions, or pull requests. These permissions can materially increase the impact of workflow compromise.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(repo:GH_Repository)-[:GH_Contains]->(:GH_Workflow)-[:GH_Contains]->(job:GH_WorkflowJob)
WHERE 'contents:write' IN job.effective_github_token_permissions
OR 'actions:write' IN job.effective_github_token_permissions
OR 'pull-requests:write' IN job.effective_github_token_permissions
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Jobs whose GITHUB_TOKEN is declared with write on contents, Actions or pull requests — the permissions that let a compromised step change code or approve itself.
gryphon: WHERE j.data.permissions.contents = "write" OR j.data.permissions.actions = "write" OR j.data.permissions["pull-requests"] = "write" OR j.data.configuration.workflow_permissions.contents = "write" OR j.data.configuration.workflow_permissions.actions = "write" OR j.data.configuration.workflow_permissions["pull-requests"] = "write"
RETURN w.data.full_name AS repository, w.data.path AS workflow, j.data.job_key AS job, j.data.permissions AS job_permissions, j.data.configuration.workflow_permissions AS workflow_permissions
queries.caveat: DECLARED permissions, on the job or inherited from the workflow. BloodHound computes the *effective* token from the repository's default-workflow-permissions policy too; that policy is not collected yet (a small follow-on to github-core#110).

queries.name: Workflow Jobs with OIDC Token Permission
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns workflow jobs whose calculated effective GITHUB_TOKEN permissions include id-token:write. These jobs can request GitHub OIDC tokens, though additional step analysis is needed to determine whether the token is actually used.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(repo:GH_Repository)-[:GH_Contains]->(:GH_Workflow)-[:GH_Contains]->(job:GH_WorkflowJob)
WHERE 'id-token:write' IN job.effective_github_token_permissions
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Jobs that may request an OIDC token — the jobs that can become a cloud identity. Whether they do is the next query.
gryphon: RETURN w.data.full_name AS repository, w.data.path AS workflow, j.data.job_key AS job, j.data.environment AS environment

queries.name: OIDC-Capable Workflow Jobs Interceptable by Self-Hosted Runners
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns OIDC-capable workflow jobs whose execution context may be exposed to an actor controlling a collected self-hosted runner that is not explicitly marked ephemeral. These jobs are especially important to review because runner compromise could expose short-lived cloud federation tokens.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(runner:GH_Runner)-[:GH_CanInterceptJob]->(job:GH_WorkflowJob)
WHERE 'id-token:write' IN job.effective_github_token_permissions
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: Interceptable jobs that can also mint a cloud identity.
queries.hatch: same runner, filtered on id-token: write

queries.name: Workflow Jobs with Observed OIDC Authentication Steps
queries.bloodhound_description: Returns OIDC-capable workflow jobs with direct descendant steps that show likely OIDC token consumption, including common AWS, Azure, GitHub Pages, and direct token-request patterns. This is evidence of likely use, not a complete classifier for every possible OIDC consumer; reusable workflow callers may require following GH_CallsWorkflow to find the consuming steps.

sources.cypher:
MATCH p=(repo:GH_Repository)-[:GH_Contains]->(:GH_Workflow)-[:GH_Contains]->(job:GH_WorkflowJob)-[:GH_Contains]->(step:GH_WorkflowStep)
WHERE 'id-token:write' IN job.effective_github_token_permissions
AND (
  step.action_slug = 'aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials'
  OR step.action_slug = 'azure/login'
  OR step.action_slug = 'Azure/login'
  OR step.action_slug = 'actions/deploy-pages'
  OR step.contents CONTAINS 'getIDToken'
  OR step.contents CONTAINS 'ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL'
  OR step.contents CONTAINS 'ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN'
)
RETURN p
LIMIT 1000

queries.about: OIDC-capable jobs that visibly exchange the token for a cloud credential — the AWS, Azure and Pages login actions. The `getIDToken` / `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` half of BloodHound's filter reads step bodies, which the grid keeps as text in `configuration.steps` and Gryphon cannot search inside arrays.
gryphon: RETURN j.data.full_name AS repository, j.data.workflow_path AS workflow, j.data.job_key AS job, act.data.action_path AS action, u.data.properties.declared_ref AS declared_ref, u.data.properties.pin_kind AS pin
